title: module trust is exact, not a prefix: a bare package whose name merely STARTS with the intrinsic letters is an ordinary untrusted foreign module and needs an initialization trust claim
notes: poc/src/language/README.md: 'Module trust is exact: only the declared compiler modules `vibelang/context`, `vibelang/provider`, `vibelang:exceptions`, `vibelang:comptime`, and `vibelang:flows` are compiler intrinsics. **Prefixes do not confer trust; every other specifier is an ordinary foreign module.**' This is a fail-open obligation with a supply-chain shape: if trust were granted by prefix, publishing a package named `vibelangutils` would be enough to have a `.vibe` program treat it as compiler-owned and skip both the module-initialization trust check (VIBE1510) and the per-call panic charge. The binding is only INSPECTED, never called, so the declared diagnostic is the module-trust rule alone rather than the VIBE1101/1301/1507/1508 foreign-call cascade a call would add on top. The coverage audit that created this area recorded the obligation as unwritable on the grounds that a bare specifier cannot resolve in the harness's flat staging directory and the case would measure resolution failure instead; that is not what happens — VIBE1510 is decided lexically from the specifier, so the rule is reached before resolution matters.
